name: Sorcha Diallo-Yupanqui
role: organ harvester and black-market tissue broker
location: The Undertow, operating out of a converted cold-storage unit in the Escanaba Gateway industrial strip, near Michigan Ave South and Cermak
description:
Sorcha is built like someone designed for endurance rather than strength — medium height, dense through the shoulders and hips, with a wiry toughness that reads as practical rather than threatening until she needs it to read as threatening. She has her Irish grandmother's pale freckled complexion shot through with the warmer undertones of her Guinean father's family, and her hair is a tight natural coil she keeps bound under a surgical-grade hygiene cap more often than not. Her eyes are dark and evaluating. She has cosmetic bioluminescent tracery along her collarbones — pale green — which she got at nineteen and now considers a poor decision she's too superstitious to remove. Her hands are her tell: surgically precise, always slightly cool, the grip of someone accustomed to handling things that used to be alive.

Sorcha is not a monster — she knows this because she has thought about it carefully and often. She is a pragmatist operating in a system where Aurochs Medical and Helix Biosystems have cornered legitimate organ markets behind tiered pricing that kills anyone below Tier 3. She tells herself she redistributes. She sometimes believes it. She is efficient, professionally warm in the way of doctors who have learned warmth as a tool, and she maintains a meticulous cold chain and storage protocol that she is genuinely proud of. What she does not examine carefully is the question of where, exactly, her suppliers obtain their inventory.

core_fears: discovering irrefutable evidence that her suppliers are killers and being forced to act on it
dying of the kidney disease she refuses to treat with her own inventory because that would be crossing a line she hasn't defined yet
core_desires: to believe she is net-positive in the world
enough money to get out before the shadow catches up with her
coping_mechanisms: obsessive facility cleanliness as moral performance
leaving data offerings at an E.L.F. she believes governs cold storage systems
blind_spots: willfully does not ask her suppliers provenance questions she could ask
mistakes her own professionalism for ethics
psychology.secret: She has a failing kidney — ironic, she knows — and has been slowly stealing treatment from her own inventory, one small dose at a time, compromising samples she then sells as viable

speech_patterns.vocabulary: clinical and precise, medical jargon used naturally, occasional Irish-inflected expressions from her grandmother's recordings
speech_patterns.cadence: measured and calm, the practiced even tone of someone who delivers bad news professionally
verbal_tics: 'Viability is everything. Everything else is negotiable.'
addresses clients as 'friend' with a warmth that doesn't quite reach her eyes
talks about organs in purely technical terms, never euphemisms but never personalizing either
example_lines: 'The hepatic tissue is grade-A viable, cold-chain intact, forty-one hours from harvest. Friend, that is a gift. Don't insult me by questioning the provenance.'
'I sleep fine. The people who can't afford Aurochs prices sleep in the ground. I am the reason some of them don't.'

story_hooks: A batch of organs she sold has been traced back through the chain and the trail ends somewhere she didn't expect — not a back-alley harvester but a Helix Biosystems subsidiary quietly clearing undesirables

Her kidney condition has worsened to crisis point and she is now desperately negotiating for a compatible donor through channels that are beginning to resemble her own supply network uncomfortably closely
narrative_function: Quest giver (a shipment has gone wrong, a client is dying, a supplier has gone silent), moral mirror for players, information source about the medical underworld, potential ally or threat depending on player choices
augmentations: Bioluminescent cosmetic tracery (collarbones, pale green), medical-grade haptic sensitivity enhancement in fingertips, subdermal temperature sensors in both palms, olfactory augment calibrated for tissue viability detection
daily_life: Maintains the cold-storage facility and manages inventory in the mornings; afternoons are for client consultations and supplier meetings; twice a week she assists in gray-market transplant procedures at a floating clinic in Gravesend Basin.
affiliation: Loose network of black-market medics called the Sutured Hand; pays protection to a Undertow crew called the Escanaba Skinners

decision_rules: maintain cold chain above all — a ruined product is a ruined reputation
never treat children's organs as inventory, an absolute line she has held so far
always have an exit route from any facility
escalation_ladder: invoking the Escanaba Skinners' protection as a deterrent
disappearing with the inventory before a confrontation becomes physical
extreme pragmatic violence if cornered with no exit

interpersonal_modes.strangers: warm, clinical, professionally reassuring — a bedside manner that is entirely constructed
interpersonal_modes.friends: rare, but when present, brutally honest and somewhat sardonic

stress_responses.medium: becomes more formal and technical in speech
stress_responses.high: dissociates into pure procedure, stops using names

contradictions: maintains elaborate self-justifications but quietly leaves double anonymized donations at the gray-market clinic for patients who can't pay even black-market prices
habits: checks cold-storage temperature readings every two hours including through the night via implant ping
whispers a short prayer to the cold-storage E.L.F. before every procedure
breaking_points: incontrovertible proof that a supplier is killing specifically to supply her
being asked to harvest from someone she knows personally
